title: One address, many roles
question: Which addresses hold a City-funded nonprofit, a contractor that it pays, and a party active in lobbying or campaign giving?
finding: 6 addresses outside the large office buildings hold a City-funded nonprofit together with a contractor or grantee paid by a City-funded nonprofit at the same address; 3 of them also hold a party that pays registered lobbyists or gives to political committees. The largest by money passed on is 934 Brannan St: Asian Pacific Islander Cultural Center, paid by Somarts: $506,437 (2021-2024); Queer Cultural Center Qcc, paid by Somarts: $287,770 (2024-2025).
how: Each organization and firm in the graph was placed at its San Francisco street address: the address on its latest tax return, its business registration with the Treasurer, or the address a paying nonprofit gives for it on a tax return. Addresses with 25 or more active business registrations, mail drops, and addresses the assessor classes as houses, condominiums or small flats were left out. An address is listed when it holds a City-funded nonprofit and a party that a City-funded nonprofit at that address pays (grant, largest contractor, rent). The political column shows any party there that pays registered lobbyists (lobbyist register) or gives to committees in its own name. The files on disk hold no street addresses for campaign committees, so a committee registered at an address cannot be seen; the committees' own registration statements with the Ethics Commission would supply them.
limits: Being linked is not being involved: nonprofits share board members, buildings and auditors all the time, and San Francisco is a small city. A group is a place to look, ranked by how many independent signs sit inside it. Declared affiliates at one address were counted once, but a landlord nonprofit and its tenants, a fiscal sponsor and its projects, or a parent and a financing subsidiary under a different name will still appear here, and those are ordinary arrangements. An address is a building, not a room: two parties at one street number may never meet. Several of these buildings are City-owned cultural or community centres, where a master tenant and its sub-tenants are placed together by the City itself; the City’s facilities list is used to label them. Same street address: nonprofit centres, landlords and tenants, and fiscal sponsors share buildings. Pays (grant, contract or rent): sub-grants and specialist contractors are how programmes are delivered. Lobbies or consults for: lobbying and permit consulting are registered and reported. Gives to the campaign of: campaign donations are reported, with limits on amounts.
